messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT P1 - multiple GPU nodes reporting rapid driver resets and ECC correctable errors, starting 1748889999. Paging on-call.
Maya R: seeing a backscatter pattern — node-gpu-12 reset -> increased ECCs on node-gpu-13/14 within ~30s. Not isolated to a single host type.
Sanjay P: @Maya R can you drop topline telemetry links? curious about mem pressure and kernel oops correlation.
Maya R: https://telemetry.internal/reports/1748889999 backscatter view + nv-host-reset counters. nv-host-reset spikes at root, then xid 43/86 messages on peers.
Eli V: copying relevant dmesg snippets:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 43, PID: 4321, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568012] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3c:00): 86, GPU exception on EFI path.
[ 1234.600001] kernel: oops in nvidia 0xdeadbeef
```
Tess L: customers on Dedicated seeing elevated error rates and some inference requests failing with 502s. CS reports Priya: 3 customers flagged in last 5m. Priya (cs): customers A and B report intermittent timeouts, one on private deployment reported container restarts.
Jordan (ops-lead): status? impact P1 but not widespread yet. Are any node-level OOMs showing? Could be driver/firmware mixed failure.
Maya R: no host OOMs. Memory usage stable. Pattern consistent with transient PCI link flaps leading to driver reset cascades. Also seeing ECC correctable spike pre-reset.
Sanjay P: immediate mitigation plan proposals:
- cordon node-gpu-12, drain affected pods
- restrict scheduling to lower-memory models on the cluster pool
- route new requests to fallback model variants
- enable kernel nv-retry/quirks? (needs infra)
Eli V: prepared drain commands:
```
kubectl cordon node-gpu-12
kubectl drain node-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
Maya R: starting cordon/drain for node-gpu-12 now. Will watch for backscatter to other nodes.
infra-bot: deploy job 174888A queued: node isolation playbook run -> will taint drained nodes with inference-critical=isolated:NoSchedule
deploy-bot: routing rule change: add fallback-model-v2 to traffic pool for affected customers. Rolling out in 2m.
Priya (cs): notifying CS escalation list + affected customers with initial incident note. ETA for customer update 15m.
Jordan (ops-lead): good. Also get gpu firmware/driver versions list for the flapping nodes. Could be regression in driver 535.x.
Maya R: driver versions on affected fleet: 525.85 (node-gpu-12), 530.10 (node-gpu-13), 530.10 (node-gpu-14). Not uniform.
Sanjay P: mismatch is suspicious. If firmware/driver mismatch -> try soft-evacuate fleet and pin to the most stable image. Ops: can we isolate nodes with mixed drivers?
Jordan (ops-lead): yes, we can quarantine mixed-driver hosts. Eli, start labeling nodes with driver version and block inference scheduling on mismatched ones.
Eli V: running label script now. Output:
```
node-gpu-12: driver=525.85
node-gpu-13: driver=530.10
node-gpu-14: driver=530.10
node-gpu-15: driver=530.10
```
Maya R: after cordon, node-gpu-12 had two successive nv-host-reset events and then kubelet restarted a container. container logs show:
```
2025-06-03T12:01:02Z inference: runtime: gpu init failed: nvidia: Xid 43
2025-06-03T12:01:03Z kubelet: container crashloop backoff
```
Sanjay P: rolling forward mitigation: take node-gpu-12 out of rotation, re-route customer traffic, and run a targeted firmware probe. If we still see ECC correctable increase on 13/14 after 12 is isolated -> escalate to hw replacement.
Maya R: isolating 12 complete. Monitoring.
(5m later)
Maya R: seeing reduced 502s for customers A/B. CS update sent. Priya: customer A acknowledged fallback, wants SLA impact estimate.
Priya (cs): requested list of affected requests and duration window. Jordan: can we generate correlation from request logs? We need token-level failure windows.
Eli V: pulled request logs for window 12:00–12:10. Linking: https://logs.internal/1748889999/requests
Maya R: telemetry shows ECC correctables spiked on node-gpu-13 right after 12 was tainted. It's a 'backscatter' — either electrical noise on shared PCI fabric or a driver race when peers reassign NV links.
Sanjay P: hardware mitigations: power-cycle the enclosure for that rack? ops to coordinate with colo. Firmware downgrade to 525 is candidate but risky.
Jordan (ops-lead): we need a short-term and long-term plan. Short-term: quarantine mixed-driver nodes, keep fallback routing and drain suspect nodes. Long-term: fleet-wide driver audit and uniformization + run kernel nv-host-reset regression test.
Tess L: open action items:
- [ ] CS update to customers with precise window (Priya)
- [ ] Quarantine mixed-driver nodes (Eli/Jordan)
- [ ] Hardware ticket to colo for enclosure power-cycle if backscatter persists (Jordan)
- [ ] Fleet driver audit (Sanjay)
- [ ] Incident blameless postmortem (Maya)
Maya R: preparing a followup runbook entry for 'ecc-backscatter' pattern: include detection queries, thresholds, drain steps, and telemetry dashboards.
infra-bot: note: automated rollback triggered for any node that hits >3 nv-host-reset events in 10m.
deploy-bot: fallback routing completed. Percent traffic shifted: 48% -> fallback-model-v2 for affected customers.
Priya (cs): customer A asked for ETA to full restoration — we can say will update in 60m after hardware verification.
Sanjay P: next steps for oncall: if backscatter continues after isolating all mixed-driver hosts -> escalate to HW + driver vendor. Collect serials and ECC logs for RMA.
Maya R: ack. Will keep thread updated. tagging @oncall for the next handoff in 30m.
Jordan (ops-lead): current scope: 4 nodes observed with resets, 3 customers affected intermittently. Severity remains P1 until stable for 30m and all affected pods on fallback.
Maya R: quick snippet for post-incident triage (for PMs): cause hypothesis = PCI fabric noise or driver regression -> symptoms = Xid 43/86 spikes, kernel oops, container restarts, cascading ECC correctable wave.
Eli V: saving logs to incident bundle: s3://incidents/1748889999/bundle.tar.gz
Maya R: handing off to @Sanjay P for next 30m watch and root cause lead. I'll update the postmortem skeleton.
Sanjay P: taking over monitoring. Will escalate to vendor with logs if we see >2 new resets. Thanks all, please react with :thumbsup: when you see handled.
Maya R: :thumbsup:
Priya (cs): :white_check_mark: customer updates sent.
oncall-bot: HANDOFF -> new oncall: Sanjay P, previous: Maya R, handoff_ts: 1748890430.
